correctionsIssued.finding: MY INSTRUCTION WAS WRONG, AND THE LANE WAS RIGHT TO REFUSE IT.
correctionsIssued.whatHappened: lane-b did not relabel and said why: `asserted` is unreachable in this corpus, not merely discouraged.
correctionsIssued.plannerCheck: I verified the claim myself at source. lib/adapters/src/local/setbacks/gate.ts:224-234 — for any state other than `primary-source-verified` the gate resolves `atom_did` and emits a BLOCK-level G2 result when it does not resolve, with the literal message `atom_did required for verification_state "asserted" but missing` (line 233). Lines 70-77 document the same asymmetry in the type: `atom_did` is omitted for `primary-source-verified` and required for `asserted`/`human-verified`, "both of which claim atom backing". Waco has no atom corpus, so no `atom_did` could resolve and relabelling would have hard-blocked all 112 values and failed CI.
correctionsIssued.consequence: The correction stands as the lane performed it. The lane additionally pinned the measurement with a test in both repos (relabel the real table `asserted`, run the gate, expect a G2 block) rather than asserting it, and raised the underlying gap as a program-level open thread: docs/setback-extraction-acceptance-gate.md rule G6 describes `asserted` as "extracted with a citation, not yet eyeballed" while gate.ts reads it as "atom-backed", and the two cannot both be the meaning. That is a corpus-level vocabulary ruling, not a lane edit, and it is carried into the close.
correctionsIssued.record: I am recording this because a lane that pushes back with a source-verified argument is doing its job, and a planner instruction that would have broken the gate is a finding about the planner, not about the lane.

A probe script crashed on the file; I then wrote _inbox/2026-09-16_p258_additivecheck.mjs, which parses both revisions of every table and compares district-by-district, because a line-grep for removed numeric lines can silently match nothing and read exactly like a pass — which is what my first attempt at this check did.

f1_undeclaredMutation.resolution: declared, not reverted, at my instruction: the change moves those four rows INTO compliance with the corpus package's own implemented G7 rule (see f3), so reverting would have re-created a latent block to fix a paperwork defect. The lane added a marked correction block to both notes, a changesToPreexistingRows block and open threads to the fragment, and a pinning test in each repo.
f1_undeclaredMutation.lesson: The wave's own verification did not detect a mutation of pre-existing data in the canonical data home. Anything that reports on what changed must be derived by parsing both revisions, not by reading a lane's summary or grepping a diff.

f2_plannerErrorsCorrectedByTheLane.whatHappened: I told lane-c that round-rock-tx.json's RULING 4 claimed a gate rule that does not exist, and that 999 is flagged out-of-band. The lane pushed back with sources and I verified both corrections myself.
f2_plannerErrorsCorrectedByTheLane.myError1: 'rule G7 does not exist.' FALSE. I grepped legacy-design-tools' gate.ts and the LDT gate doc (0 hits each) and never looked at the corpus package's own gate. Verified after the lane's push-back: hauska-setback-corpus/src/setbacks/gate.ts carries `G7` in the rule union (line 137), `export const NOT_SPECIFIED_MAX_HEIGHT_FT = 999` (line 70), and a G7 implementation at lines 307-324 that blocks a max_height_ft flagged not_specified whose value is not 999. RULING 4's sentence was false for the LDT copy of the file and true for the corpus copy.
f2_plannerErrorsCorrectedByTheLane.myError2: 'G3 flags 999 as outside SANITY_BOUNDS.max_height_ft [0,300].' FALSE. The band check is guarded by `if (!isNotSpecified)` (LDT gate.ts:259), so a not_specified cell never reaches the band check. The lane asserted this executably rather than in prose, by running the real gate over exactly those four rows.
f2_plannerErrorsCorrectedByTheLane.record: This is the second time in this wave that a lane corrected me with a source-verified argument, and both times the lane was right (the first was lane-b refusing my `asserted` relabel, which gate.ts:233 would have blocked). I verified each after the fact rather than accepting it. Recording it because it is the strongest evidence available about how this wave's verification actually worked: the lanes checked the planner, not only the reverse, and the planner's own claims were not exempt from being wrong.

f3_theRealGapAndTheRealNumbers.finding: G7 is implemented and unit-tested in the corpus package, and is never exercised against the shipped tables. So the invariant RULING 4 says 'is checked in code, not left to a convention' is checked in a test and unchecked in the corpus.

f3_theRealGapAndTheRealNumbers.theAmbiguityUnderneath: The same flag means at least two different things in shipped data. austin-tx.json's SF-1 carries max_height_ft=35 with verification_state `asserted` and a real atom_did, and its max_height_ft provenance sets not_specified: true — where the flag cannot mean 'no value stated', because a real 35-foot limit is stated. G7 assumes the flag always means 'honest gap, so the value must be the 999 sentinel'. Both readings are in the corpus at once, which is why a rule that looks purely mechanical would block 120 rows that nobody currently believes are wrong.
f3_theRealGapAndTheRealNumbers.consequence: Carried into the close as the wave's most consequential program-level finding, for the corpus owners rather than for this wave. This wave does not re-label any of those rows and does not run G7 over shipped tables.

f4_sentinelConventionSpread.finding: The wave introduced the numeric 999 sentinel into four files that had none on main: austin (0 -> 4 cells), waco (0 -> 4), san-marcos (0 -> 6, of which 4 are the declared edit in f1), kyle (0 -> 1). 21 new cells in total carry 999, all with not_specified: true.
f4_sentinelConventionSpread.why: Each lane followed round-rock-tx.json's RULING 4, the one file that already used 999, rather than a corpus-wide ruling — because for a not-specified height there was no in-file precedent to follow (austin's 36 pre-existing not_specified flags sit on other fields).
f4_sentinelConventionSpread.status: left standing deliberately. Choosing between the numeric sentinel (999), the string sentinel (`NOT_SPECIFIED = 'not_specified'`) and the older plain 100 for a not-specified height is a corpus-level vocabulary ruling, and CP2's own lesson is that a planner instruction in this area can break the gate. It is named as an open thread, not fixed from one lane.

methodChangesForBatch2: Cite the route, not just the URL. Batch 1 produced two citations that a second party could not reproduce (a browser-rendered Municode page; a dead third-party mirror). Batch 2 must record HOW the text was read whenever a plain fetch does not return it, and must prefer an authoritative-but-hard-to-reproduce citation over a fetchable-but-stale one.

`verification_state` is a gate constraint before it is a claim. `primary-source-verified` is the only state reachable without a code-section atom corpus; `asserted` requires a resolving `atom_did` and BLOCKS without one (gate.ts:233). So the label cannot carry the honesty by itself: every batch-2 row needs a note saying what was actually read, what was not, and which source kind it was.

Budget for walls. In one batch the wave hit Municode 403, an ArcGIS token wall, an AmLegal Cloudflare wall, eCode360 per-document timeouts, a Cloudflare-fronted third-party mirror and an OCR-mirrored PDF. For the no-table half — 54 cities, mostly small, many with no online code at all — a wall is the expected outcome, and the deliverable is then a SOURCED declared-unacquirable note naming what was tried, not a row.

Check the instrument's vintage before extracting. lane-c's Bastrop finding is the model: the city repealed its zoning code and adopted a Development Code, so the table's ten rows are retired-scheme names, the five codes the census called missing exist as real chart scalars, and yet the right answer was still to add no rows — because those codes are served from a hash-locked table in another repo, and promoting them is a policy change with a cross-repo lock update, not a research gap. The lane withdrew rows it had briefly written and recorded the chart values as evidence instead. Batch 2 must ask "which instrument is in force, and who owns the table that serves this code?" before writing a row.

Classification is the deliverable for the no-table half. 54 of 61 batch-1 city rows did not exist; batch 1's district half still produced 138 non-acquired units (36 declared-unacquirable, 51 blocked). Batch 2 should expect declared-unacquirable and blocked to be the majority outcome, and an outcome of mostly-declined with sources beats a handful of thin rows.

Do not research a city twice. 61 rows are 54 distinct cities. A city spanning counties is researched once by the lane owning its heaviest row; the other rows carry `researchedIn` and take the same state.
